source: Create a realistic city driving map for a car game. The city should have a grid layout of streets with the following elements: - A ground/base plate representing asphalt roads forming a grid pattern with intersections - Buildings of varying heights on the blocks between roads (some tall, some medium, some short) - Sidewalks along the edges of roads - Road markings (lane dividers, crosswalks at intersections) - Street lights at intersections - Trees or small vegetation on some sidewalks - Parking lots or open spaces in some blocks Make it look realistic with appropriate colors: dark gray asphalt, gray sidewalks, varied building colors (browns, grays, blues), green trees. Expose the following configurable attributes: - blockSize: size of each city block (controls building area) - roadWidth: width of the roads - gridCount: number of blocks in the grid (controls overall map size) - buildingHeightMin: minimum building height - buildingHeightMax: maximum building height - treeDensity: how many trees to place along sidewalks - streetLightSpacing: distance between street lights
scene_prompt: Create a realistic 3D city driving map organized as a grid of asphalt streets and intersections. City blocks between the roads contain buildings of varied heights—tall, medium, and short—in brown, gray, and blue tones, with some blocks used for parking lots or open open spaces. Gray sidewalks border every road, with green trees or small vegetation placed along selected sidewalks. Use dark gray asphalt with lane dividers and crosswalks at intersections, and place street lights at intersections. Size the overall grid, blocks, roads, building-height range, tree density, and street-light spacing to be configurable.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Simulation, specifically a vehicle-driving map without a stated race, lap, or finish condition. No secondary genre applies.

### Shape and preset
Use `world-shared`: one contiguous city street network that vehicles can traverse freely. The closest preset is Vehicle Sim, but its shared-resource-field option is not part of this prompt, so the preset is `none`; retain only its shared-world driving form.

### Config requirements
Use visible-geometry option `path-road-vehicle` for a connected, vehicle-width orthogonal street grid with intersections, lane corridors, and turning space. Use visible-geometry universal option `settlement-density` for dense city blocks populated by varied-height buildings, parking lots, and occasional open parcels. No invisible layout options are required. Keep block size, road width, grid count, minimum and maximum building height, tree density, and street-light spacing as adjustable dimensional parameters; they control the stated geometry rather than appearing as UI.

### Layout components
Build a single rectangular city zone organized as an adjustable grid of dark-gray asphalt roads. Each road segment meets at clear four-way intersections and is bordered by gray sidewalks. Mark roads with lane dividers and place crosswalks across every intersection. Set street lights at intersections, with optional intermediate lights governed by the adjustable spacing. Fill the blocks between roads with a varied skyline of tall, medium, and short brown, gray, and blue buildings. Reserve some complete or partial blocks for paved parking lots and open spaces. Distribute green trees and small vegetation along selected sidewalk runs according to the adjustable density. The road grid is the primary circulation network, with parking and open blocks breaking up building mass. Keep the outer city edge as the map boundary, visually closed by a continuation of perimeter buildings or distant urban backdrop. Compose the scene from an elevated three-quarter view that clearly shows the street lattice, intersections, sidewalks, and height variation.

### Render order
Use `topdown`: the connected street grid and intersection topology must be established in plan before the isometric city dressing is generated.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Use a medium scale, driven by the configurable grid count and block dimensions. Theme: realistic contemporary urban driving district, dark asphalt, neutral concrete, muted brown/gray/blue buildings, and green roadside planting. Pipeline modifier: `P0`, because this is one contiguous, single-surface outdoor city with no stacked roads, interiors, separate maps, or volumetric traversal.
